Name: Acre (עכו)
Description: A Hellenistic aqueduct consisting of tunnels and shafts, approximately 13 km long, built in the 3rd century BCE.

Name: Athens (Acropolis) (אתונה (יוון))
Description: A clay pipe and tunnel system, 17 km long, built in the 6th century BCE.

Name: Olynthus (אולינתוס)
Description: An underground aqueduct, 13 km long, built in the 5th century BCE.

Name: Rome (Anio Vetus) (רומא (אניו וטוס))
Description: The Anio Vetus, an underground aqueduct, 64 km long, built in 272 BCE.

Name: Rome (Aqua Appia) (רומא (אקווה אפיה))
Description: The Aqua Appia, an underground aqueduct, 17.6 km long, built in 312 BCE.

Name: Rome (Aqua Marcia) (רומא (אקווה מרקיה))
Description: The Aqua Marcia, an aqueduct 91 km long (10 km on arches), built between 144-140 BCE, supplying water to Rome.

Name: Samos (Eupalinos Tunnel) (מנהרת אופלינוס (סמוס))
Description: The Eupalinos Tunnel, a 2 km long tunnel with 60 shafts, built in 524 BCE.

Name: Sidon (צידון)
Description: An underground aqueduct and tunnel with shafts, 24 km long, dating to the 6th century BCE.
